children: Shares of Corvex were higher after the company signed a $103 million take-or-pay agreement to provide Nvidia Blackwell computing capacity to a scaled artificial intelligence inference platform.
Shares of Corvex increased 9.6% to $4.90 on Monday. The stock is down 20% year to date.
As part of the three-year agreement, the AI cloud computing company will deliver more than 1,000 Nvidia HGX B200 systems connected with the Nvidia Quantum-2 InfiniBand networking platform.
After the deployment's completion, Corvex expects contracted take-or-pay annual recurring revenue at its mid-atlantic data center to increase from $22 million to about $56 million.

The deployment, including GPU servers, storage, networking and spares, is expected to cost about $78 million, Corvex said. The customer and a lender will fund more than 80% of the cost of deployment, which is expected to begin generating revenue by the end of the first quarter of 2027. Corvex intends to fund the remaining $14 million.
The deal marks Corvex's third Nvidia Blackwell deployment at this mid-Atlantic data center.
